To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel trainable local descriptor, which is based on a deep neural network and that we show that this approach outperforms the widely used Sift descriptor.
we propose a new approach for learning descriptors for recognition and that the learned descriptors perform better than SIFT.
1) we propose to learn descriptors by using convolutional neural networks and 2) the learned descriptors outperform the state-of-the-art descriptors for the object recognition task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) What is the impact of the training data on the recognition performance of the learned local descriptors?
the following questions: 1) How to learn local descriptors?
the question whether it is possible to learn local descriptors for recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach performs better than SIFT in terms of accuracy, but is also more expensive in terms of computation time.
the proposed method performs well on the considered datasets and that the performance can be further increased by using a more sophisticated neural network architecture.
the learned descriptors outperform SIFT in the majority of experiments and the learned descriptors are more robust to changes in illumination, viewpoint and scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method can be seen as a generalization of the SIFT method.
the learned descriptors are more distinctive than SIFT and that they can be made more invariant by training.
the proposed method outperforms the SIFT approach on the task of object recognition, but not on the task of image retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method outperforms the SIFT method for a variety of tasks, e.g., object recognition, structure from motion, and stereo matching.
trainable descriptors can outperform hand-crafted ones, even if the training data is synthetically generated.
learned local descriptors outperform SIFT in terms of recognition accuracy.
